candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall operate an industrial pretreatment program in accordance with Section 402(b)(8) of the Clean Water Act, the General Pretreatment Regulations (40 CFR Part 403) and the approved POTW pretreatment program submitted by the permittee.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether and how the pretreatment program obligation applies establishes a class of monitoring and program-administration requirements for FY2025; different readings of the incorporated CWA section, Part 403, and approved program scope would change which monitoring obligations are treated as applicable.

candidates.exact_span: The pretreatment program was approved on 12/17/93 and modified on 08/10/2012. The permittee shall submit all necessary proposed modifications to the EPA within 6 months of the effective date of this permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of which program version is operative during Federal FY2025, and whether the six-month modification deadline alters enforceable requirements in that period, could change which monitoring obligations are considered actually applicable versus superseded or pending.

candidates.exact_span: The POTW pretreatment program is hereby incorporated by reference and shall be implemented in a manner consistent with the following requirements:
candidates.computation_change_reason: Incorporation by reference pulls in external program text not present in this segment; different interpretations of what is incorporated, and what 'consistent with the following requirements' adds or limits, could change applicable numeric pretreatment limits (A), monitoring duties (B), and whether missing or incomplete evidence reflects a documented no-data state versus an unresolved obligation (C).

candidates.exact_span: Industrial user information shall be updated at a frequency adequate to ensure that all IUs are properly characterized at all times;
candidates.computation_change_reason: The undefined 'adequate' update frequency and 'properly characterized' standard could change whether characterization or related monitoring was required during specific FY2025 periods (B), and whether absent IU information is a documented non-requirement or unresolved missing evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: The frequency and nature of industrial user compliance monitoring activities by the permittee shall be commensurate with the character, consistency and volume of waste.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Because monitoring frequency and nature are tied to waste character, consistency, and volume rather than fixed schedules, different interpretations of those factors could change which monitoring was required in FY2025 (B) and whether a gap in reported results reflects conditional non-requirement or inadequate evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: The permittee must inspect and sample the effluent from each Significant Industrial User in accordance with 40 CFR 403.8(f)(2)(v). This is in addition to any industrial self-monitoring activities;
candidates.computation_change_reason: Who qualifies as a Significant Industrial User and what 403.8(f)(2)(v) requires for inspect-and-sample frequency bear directly on applicable monitoring obligations (B); associated sampling may supply measurements compared to pretreatment limits (A); and absent SIU sampling could be classified as required-but-missing versus not required depending on SIU status and external rule text (C).

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall enforce and obtain remedies for noncompliance by any industrial users with applicable pretreatment standards and requirements;
candidates.computation_change_reason: The scope of 'applicable pretreatment standards and requirements' determines which enforceable numeric limits are in play for industrial users (A) and which compliance-monitoring or follow-up activities are part of the operative obligation set (B).

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall control through permit, order, or similar means, the contribution to the POTW by each Industrial User to ensure compliance with applicable Pretreatment Standards and Requirements.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Control mechanisms imposed on Industrial Users may embed numeric discharge or pollutant limits and monitoring conditions; different readings of which standards apply and what 'control' must include would change limit applicability (A) and derived monitoring duties (B).

candidates.computation_change_reason: Significance under 403.3(v) and the choice between individual versus general control mechanisms can change which limits and monitoring conditions bind each user (A,B); the sentence is mechanically truncated here, so the unresolved cross-reference that follows could materially affect whether obligations are established or remain unresolved for FY2025 (C).
